title.suggested: Hogan's Omaha doctor says the Allen fight was fixed; Allen responds

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat printed a card from Omaha doctor C. E. Tennent saying Ben Hogan never meant to fight Tom Allen and the fight was arranged as a draw. Allen told a reporter Hogan had not been fouled.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Wednesday, December 10, 1873'

facts.fact: Dr. C. E. Tennent of Omaha, who had certified that Hogan was struck below the belt, published a card saying Ben Hogan never intended to fight Allen, was physically unfit, and that it was arranged on the train that the ropes be cut and the fight made a draw
Allen said he had told Dr. Tennent he would lose nothing if he told the truth about the Hogan fight
facts.quote: No; I sent to him to tell him that if he told the truth about the fight, I would see that he didn't lose anything.
Me hit Hogan foul, indeed! Why I made up my mind not to hit that plaster if they put it around his neck.

facts.fact: Allen trained near Omaha before the Hogan fight

notes: Allen also says the Police Court cases over the Wash Home chase after Hogan were dismissed (see 502). Fact 4 rests on Allen saying the doctor 'came out to see me when I was near Omaha at work'.
